header:
Date: 2026-12-08 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ethan Brooks (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (MiraHealth CTO), Carlos Gomez (Lead ML Eng), Lina Patel (Infra), Anita Rao (Product), Speaker 1 (PM)
Recording: Fireflies auto-transcript
Purpose: Weekly POC readout — latency/throughput review vs incumbent baseline, routing and quantization tuning, next steps
summary: This was a technical POC check-in to review week-3 lab benchmarks comparing Redwood's inference configuration to incumbent provider. Redwood presented tuned batching and int8 quantization results showing improved p95 latency and higher sustained throughput for our workload; customer raised questions about cold-starts, tail-latency, KV/prefix cache behavior, and VPC security. Action items were assigned for a 48-hour A/B soak and additional infra tests. The team agreed to a security deep-dive next week and Redwood requested a short dedicated slot for a 24-hour soak test.
topics: quantization int8 vs fp16 quality tradeoffs
prefix/KV caching and warm vs cold behavior
security: KMS, VPC peering, audit logs
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hi everyone, thank you for joining. Quick roll call, uh, Ethan and I from Redwood.
[00:06] Priya Nair: Hi Priya here, Carlos, Lina and Anita on the call.
[00:10] Maya Chen: Great. Today's focus — week three lab readout, we ran the tuned configs against the baseline you shared, and we also did a few routing variations. Ethan, want to walk the numbers?
[00:21] Ethan Brooks: Yep. I'll start with a top-line. We ran three 6-hour windows: baseline traffic replay against IncumbentCloudAI, Redwood default runtime (fp16, auto-batching), and then our tuned run (int8 quant + contiguous batching + prefix cache enabled).
[00:36] Carlos Gomez: Quick question, when you say prefix cache did you mean prefix/KV cache or just prefix?
[00:40] Ethan Brooks: Good call — prefix plus KV cache. We cached the conversation KV for repeated contexts to reduce decode steps for warm requests.
[00:45] [00:45] Priya Nair: Ok, go on.
[00:46] Ethan Brooks: So for your traffic profile — shorter prompts, average sequence length 128 tokens, 90th percentile 240 — our tuned config achieved p50 38 ms, p95 120 ms, p99 260 ms. Baseline provider p50 46 ms, p95 180 ms, p99 420 ms. Throughput sustained at 210 RPS for our config vs 150 RPS for baseline, measured on comparable GPU types.
[01:12] Carlos Gomez: Those p99 numbers look promising. What GPU did you use?
[01:15] Ethan Brooks: We used A100s in the lab cluster, same generation as baseline, same mem config. Note: we also tested a T4-like profile for cost parity and saw similar relative gains but absolute latency higher.
[01:25] Lina Patel: Are those steady-state numbers or after a cold start?
[01:28] Ethan Brooks: Those are steady-state warm windows after a 20-minute warmup. For cold-starts, p95 spikes to ~900 ms with fp16 and ~680 ms with int8 because quantized kernels warm up differently — we included those charts in the perf sheet.
[01:41] Anita Rao: Any quality differences with int8? Our product team is worried about subtle hallucination regressions.
[01:45] Ethan Brooks: We ran your 500-example eval set. BLEU-ish and custom similarity metrics stayed within your acceptance band; 4 examples out of 500 had minor formatting differences. We can share the eval diff CSV.
[01:56] [01:56] Priya Nair: Please share. We want to review with the PMs.
[01:58] Maya Chen: We'll push the eval diffs and the raw token-level traces to the drive link after the call.
[02:04] Ethan Brooks: On throughput tuning — the sweet spot for your workload was batch size 8 with dynamic batching timeout 12ms and token-parallel decode threads set to 4. Larger batches improved GPU utilization but increased p95 noticeably for short prompts.
[02:18] Carlos Gomez: You mentioned token-parallel decode threads — is that a Redwood runtime flag we can change in Dedicated?
[02:22] Ethan Brooks: Yes, that's exposed in the model runtime config. In Dedicated it maps to the kernel selection path — you can set decode parallelism up to 8 depending on core counts.
[02:30] [02:30] Speaker 1: There was a note about routing — can you explain the fallback policy?
[02:33] Maya Chen: Sure, we implemented a routing experiment: primary route to tuned int8 variant; fallback to fp16 variant if latency SLO is violated for 10 consecutive requests or if GPU queue depth > threshold. In practice, we saw 3% fallback events during a synthetic spike test with 5x burst traffic.
[02:49] Lina Patel: How do those fallback events show up in logs? We need that for our observability team.
[02:53] Ethan Brooks: They show as route_decision=FALLBACK in the trace, with the chosen model_id and a reason field. We also emit token-level cost deltas and sfr (server frame) timings.
[03:02] Carlos Gomez: Regarding the KV cache — how do you handle invalidation when context changes? We had cache staleness before.
[03:07] Ethan Brooks: We support per-session TTL and explicit invalidation API. For the tests we used TTL 300s and invalidated on session boundary. We logged a small number of stale hits during the synthetic churn test — about 0.4% — because of session ID collisions in the replay data.
[03:21] [03:21] Priya Nair: On security — we need KMS integration and proof of audit logs. Is Redwood-managed KMS ok or do we bring our own?
[03:28] Maya Chen: Both. For Private deployments you can BYOK/KMS. Hosted has optional CMKs via partner KMS. We'll schedule a security deep dive with our compliance engineer next week to run the SOC2/ISO artifacts.
[03:40] Anita Rao: Also need data residency notes — some of our EU users must remain in region.
[03:43] Maya Chen: Noted. We ran the EU-region test during the second window; latency delta was +12ms p95 due to region hop; we'll include that in the sheet.
[03:52] Ethan Brooks: Back to perf — we also measured GPU util across runs. Tuned run increased sustained GPU utilization from 58% to 78% with no OOMs. Baseline provider saw 64% util. Memory headroom stayed steady.
[04:04] Carlos Gomez: Any guidance on autoscaling thresholds if we migrate to Dedicated?
[04:08] Ethan Brooks: For your target 200–240 RPS, we recommend a min pool of 4 GPUs with scale-up threshold at 70% queue depth and scale-down cooldown of 5 min. That keeps tail-latency under 300 ms during 2x bursts.
[04:21] [04:21] Priya Nair: What about cost delta? How much cheaper is this per token?
[04:24] Maya Chen: Rough numbers from lab pricing: tuned int8 path reduces GPU token cost ~28% vs baseline fp16 path when accounting for higher throughput. We'll send a per-token cost spreadsheet for your finance team.
[04:36] Carlos Gomez: There was earlier mention of kernel selection — is Redwood using Triton or custom kernels?
[04:40] Ethan Brooks: It's a mix — custom fused attention kernels plus Triton for other parts. For quantized int8 we use optimized fused paths that reduce memory bandwidth. That's where the p95 gains come from.
[04:52] Lina Patel: For the dedicated slot soak — what exactly are we asking for?
[04:56] Maya Chen: We requested a 24-hour dedicated slot — single-customer reserved capacity to run a full production-like soak with your live-ish traffic replay to validate QoS, billing, and telemetry. It helps catch scheduling edge cases.
[05:06] Speaker 1: Any risks for the soak?
[05:08] Ethan Brooks: The main risks are missed edge prompts with extremely long sequences — those will push memory and might cause fallback. We'll flag those requests and recommend per-request max_token limits for the soak.
[05:19] [05:19] Anita Rao: On eval diffs — can you annotate the four problematic examples with root-cause? Was it quant noise or prompt truncation?
[05:27] Ethan Brooks: Initial analysis points to tokenization differences in a couple of prompts and one case of a temperature/bias mismatch in the sampling config. We'll annotate.
[05:34] Priya Nair: Ok. For the 48-hour A/B, what are the metrics we should capture?
[05:38] Maya Chen: Minimum set: p50/p95/p99 latency, request success (HTTP 200/5xx), GPU util, queue depth, cost per 1k tokens, model output quality diffs on sampled subset, number of fallback events, and cold-start frequency.
[05:51] Carlos Gomez: Can Redwood push a sidecar exporter for Prometheus so we can ingest metrics into our Grafana?
[05:55] Ethan Brooks: Yes — we can run an exporter or wire into your metrics pipeline via pushgateway. We'll provide the spec.
[05:59] [05:59] Priya Nair: I have one concern — incident handling. If we see regressions during the soak, what's the rollback path?
[06:04] Maya Chen: Rollback is immediate routing change: switch traffic back to baseline model variant or route to Incumbent provider per the failover policy. We can automate canary to 10% then roll back to 0% if metric thresholds breach.
[06:16] Anita Rao: Good. Are we tracking SLOs as part of the test?
[06:19] Ethan Brooks: Yep, we'll track SLO breaches and surface alerts. For the soak we'll set the SLO at p95 < 350 ms and success rate > 99.7% as a starting point.
[06:29] Maya Chen: Quick pause — any blockers from the infra side for the dedicated slot? Lina?
[06:33] Lina Patel: we need a short firewall window and KMS access tested; otherwise infra is OK. We'll try to have the firewall rule open by Friday.
[06:41] [06:41] Carlos Gomez: One more detail — how does Redwood charge for dedicated slot soak? Is it billed pro-rated?
[06:45] Maya Chen: For POC dedicated slot we offer a complimentary 24-hour soak once per trial, otherwise it's on the reserved capacity pricing pro-rate. Finance can confirm but we don't charge for this early validation.
[06:55] Priya Nair: Great, that helps.
[06:57] Ethan Brooks: On the A/B plan timeline — we propose starting the 48-hour A/B after we share tuned configs and you provide the production-like traffic profile. That gives us a 48–72 hour turnaround to wire the exporter and schedule the soak.
[07:11] [07:11] Anita Rao: Can you also include a small script to drive burst patterns? We want to replicate our weekend spikes.
[07:16] Ethan Brooks: We'll include a load script and a traffic pattern generator with ramp and spike phases.
[07:21] Maya Chen: Ok let's go through quick recaps and owners. Maya will share configs and perf sheet by Friday. Ethan will run the A/B once Carlos uploads the replay. Carlos to upload traffic profile and sample keys. Lina to open firewall rule.
[07:33] Priya Nair: Sounds good. Any last minute QA?
[07:35] Carlos Gomez: One tiny ask — can you include the Opentelemetry trace IDs in the perf sheet?
[07:38] Ethan Brooks: Yes, we'll include trace IDs and example spans.
[07:41] [07:41] Speaker 1: Thanks everyone.
[07:42] Maya Chen: Thanks, we'll follow up with the drive link and the action-item list.
[07:46] Priya Nair: Thanks, appreciate it.
[07:47] [07:47] Meeting ended
notes: Drive link placeholder: (will be shared post-call) contains: perf_sheet.csv, eval_diffs.csv, tuned_config.yaml, load_script.py. Security deep-dive to be scheduled with compliance engineer. Redwood to request 24h dedicated slot for soak.
